title: Pointwise finite ultrametric cochain series sum continuously before completion
statement:
Let $V$ be a normed field, meaning a field [def-weil-field] with a multiplicative real-valued absolute value and metric $d(v,w)=|v-w|$, satisfying $|v+w|\leq\max(|v|,|w|)$. No completeness of $V$ is assumed. Let $\iota:V\hookrightarrow\widehat V$ be its isometric field embedding into the complete normed field [lem-sfb-normed-field-completion]. Let $S$ be a profinite space (compact Hausdorff with clopen basis), $G$ a profinite group (compact Hausdorff with open normal subgroup basis), and $n\geq1$, using [def-weil-size-convention]. Write $C^r(P,G;V)=C(P\times G^r,V)$ for all continuous maps, with trivial group action, $d^0=0$, and for $r\geq1$
$$(dc)(s;g_1,\ldots,g_{r+1})=c(s;g_2,\ldots,g_{r+1})+\sum_{a=1}^r(-1)^a c(s;g_1,\ldots,g_ag_{a+1},\ldots,g_{r+1})+(-1)^{r+1}c(s;g_1,\ldots,g_r).$$
Let $b_i\in C^{n-1}(S,G;V)$, $i\geq0$, satisfy $\|b_i\|_\infty\to0$ and, for each fixed $(s,x)$, $b_i(s,x)=0$ for all sufficiently large $i$. Then the partial sums $b^{(N)}=\sum_{i=0}^N b_i$ converge uniformly in $\widehat V$; their limit is $\iota\circ b$ for the pointwise finite sum $b(s,x)=\sum_i b_i(s,x)\in V$. The function $b:S\times G^{n-1}\to V$ is continuous in the original norm topology, the same partial sums converge uniformly to it in $V$, and
$$\|b-b^{(N)}\|_\infty\leq\sup_{i>N}\|b_i\|_\infty.$$
If $e_i=db_i$ and the partial sums $\sum_{i=0}^N e_i$ converge uniformly to $z\in C^n(S,G;V)$, then $db=z$. This includes $n=1$ with $d^0=0$ and the empty $S$, with all supremum norms of its functions understood as zero.

proof.text: Put $X=S\times G^{n-1}$ and $a_i=\|b_i\|_\infty$. Since $a_i\to0$, the nonnegative real sequence $a_i$ is bounded (bound a finite initial segment and use $a_i<1$ afterwards). Thus $t_N=\sup_{i>N}a_i$ exists and is finite. Given $\epsilon>0$, eventually all $a_i<\epsilon/2$, so eventually $0\le t_N\le\epsilon/2<\epsilon$; hence $t_N\to0$. Induction on the number of summands gives $|\sum_{j\in F}v_j|\le\max_{j\in F}|v_j|$ for nonempty finite $F$: the induction step is exactly the assumed two-term ultrametric inequality. The empty sum has norm zero.

proof.text: For each $x\in X$, choose $K_x$ with $b_i(x)=0$ for $i>K_x$ and define $b(x)=\sum_{i=0}^{K_x}b_i(x)$. Adding zero terms makes this independent of the choice. For any $N$, $b(x)-b^{(N)}(x)$ is the finite sum over $N<i\le\max(N,K_x)$. Step 1 bounds its norm by $t_N$, independently of $x$. Taking the supremum proves the claimed tail inequality and uniform convergence in $V$. In particular $|b(x)|\le\max(a_0,t_0)$, so this supremum norm and the difference norms are finite.

source.place: Paragraph (3), open-direct-image scalar input; agent analytic expansion: pointwise finite construction and tail estimate

proof.text: Fix $x\in X$ and $\epsilon>0$. Each $b^{(N)}$ is continuous: intersect the finitely many neighborhoods where $|b_i(y)-b_i(x)|<\epsilon$ for $0\le i\le N$ and apply the finite ultrametric inequality. Choose $N$ with $t_N<\epsilon$, and a neighborhood where $|b^{(N)}(y)-b^{(N)}(x)|<\epsilon$. On it, write $b(y)-b(x)$ as $(b-b^{(N)})(y)+(b^{(N)}(y)-b^{(N)}(x))+(b^{(N)}-b)(x)$. All three terms have norm less than $\epsilon$, so their sum does too. This proves continuity in the original norm topology, without a completeness hypothesis.

source.place: Paragraph (3), open-direct-image scalar input; agent analytic expansion: original-field continuity

proof.text: The embedding supplied by [lem-sfb-normed-field-completion] is an isometry and a ring homomorphism. Consequently the partial sums of $\iota\circ b_i$ equal $\iota\circ b^{(N)}$ and $|\iota(b(x))-\iota(b^{(N)}(x))|=|b(x)-b^{(N)}(x)|\le t_N$. They therefore converge uniformly in $\widehat V$ to $\iota\circ b$, as required.

proof.text: For $r=n-1\ge1$, every term of $dh$ is a signed value of $h$, so the displayed differential and the finite ultrametric inequality imply $\|dh\|_\infty\le\|h\|_\infty$. Expanding the same finite formula gives $d(b-b^{(N)})=db-\sum_{i=0}^Ndb_i$. Thus $\|db-\sum_{i=0}^Ne_i\|_\infty\le t_N$. Since these sums also converge uniformly to $z$, at each point $|db-z|\le\max(t_N,|\sum_{i=0}^Ne_i-z|)$ tends to zero, proving $db=z$. The cochain $db$ is continuous: the argument maps in each term of $d$ are continuous projections or use continuous multiplication in $G$; the finite-neighborhood argument of step 3 handles their signed sum.

source.place: Paragraph (3), open-direct-image scalar input; agent analytic expansion: finite differential estimate and equality of limits

proof.text: If $n=1$, the preceding summation and continuity arguments apply to $X=S\times G^0=S$. Here $db=d^0b=0$ and every $e_i=0$, so uniform convergence forces $z=0$, giving $db=z$. If $S$ is empty, all functions involved are the unique empty functions, all norms are zero by the stated convention, and every asserted continuity, convergence, bound and equality holds.

Source: main-20261015 direct-images proof paragraph (3) is about proper and open direct images preserving D_ctf and has no summation argument, so the agent origin and the 'motivation only' place are accurate. The only citer is lem-sfb-prime-to-ell-cochain-finite-quotient-descent, step 5. Its step 4 supplies continuous b_i in C^{n-1}(S_0,G;Ω) with db_i=e_i, ||b_i||->0 and each b_i(s,x) eventually zero; S_0 and G are profinite, and the sums of e_i converge uniformly to z_0 in the noncomplete Ω. So every hypothesis is met, and the differential and d^0=0 convention are written exactly as in the citer. Step checks: (1) t_N=sup_{i>N}||b_i|| tends to 0, and the ultrametric bound on finite sums follows by induction; ||b_i|| is finite because X is compact (implicit, advisory only). (2) b is the pointwise finite sum, and each tail is a finite sum with norm at most t_N, which gives the stated bound without completeness. (3) Continuity in V follows from an ε/3 argument with the ultrametric inequality. (4) lem-sfb-normed-field-completion is used only for 'ring homomorphism and isometry', which its statement says, with matching hypotheses (no completeness). (5) ||dh||<=||h|| since each sign has |±1|=1; by linearity ||db-ΣΣ_{i<=N}e_i||<=t_N, hence db=z. (6) For n=1, d^0=0 forces z=0; empty S is trivial. Small cases tested: n=1, empty S, finitely many nonzero b_i, V=Ω, characteristic 2.
